## What (EI-13245)

`ptool work_items:burn_down --json='{"harness":"papercusp","ids":[...]}'`
threw:

```
MCP error -32600: Tool work_items:burn_down has an output schema but did not return structured content
```

This is a **client-side** check inside the official
`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`'s `Client.callTool()`: if the tool's cached
`tools/list` entry carries an `outputSchema`, the response **must** include a
`structuredContent` field (unless `isError`) — checked purely from field
presence, never by inspecting `content[]`.

## The two-layer bug

1. **`ptool.mjs` never requested it.** `Client.callTool()`'s validator fires
   whenever the tool has `outputSchema`, *regardless* of whether the caller
   opted in — but the operator's MCP host only *fills* `structuredContent`
   when `_meta.structured` (or `?structured=1`) is set (P-010, to avoid
   paying for both the compact text AND the full JSON on every call). Fixed
   by making `buildCallToolParams` in `ptool.mjs` always send
   `_meta: { structured: true }` — ptool is a human/scripting CLI, not a
   token-metered LLM session, so it can always afford it.

2. **The opt-in itself was broken — this was the actual root cause.**
   Even after (1), the bug still reproduced live. `serializeToolResponse`
   (`libs/generic/tooldef/src/serialize-result.ts`) only attached
   `structuredContent` when `chosen.format !== 'json'`:

   ```ts
   if (opts.includeStructured && hasData && chosen.format !== 'json') {
     result.structuredContent = data;
   }
   ```

   The reasoning ("the text body already IS the lossless JSON, so
   `structuredContent` would just duplicate it") conflates two different
   things: `content[0].text` (what the model reads) and `structuredContent`
   (a distinct MCP response field the SDK validates independently). For any
   tool whose result is an **object-rooted, non-tabular shape** (like
   `work_items:burn_down`'s nested census), TOON/CSV never beat plain JSON,
   so `chosen.format` resolves to `'json'` — which silently defeated the
   opt-in on *every* call, no matter what the caller asked for.

## The fix

Drop the `chosen.format !== 'json'` condition entirely — `structuredContent`
is attached whenever the caller opted in (`opts.includeStructured`) and there
is data, full stop:

```ts
if (opts.includeStructured && hasData) {
  result.structuredContent = data;
  _meta.structured = true;
}
```

This is the **single shared serializer** — both the HTTP operator MCP
transport (`_mcp-handler.ts`, used by `?superuser=1` sessions incl. ptool)
and the stdio `agent-mcp` server import the exact same function, so this one
fix covers every transport. No per-tool patch was needed or wanted.

## Why this only bites object-rooted tools

`outputSchema` is advertised in `tools/list` (`tool-projection.ts`) **only**
when `tool.outputJsonSchema.type === 'object'` — array/scalar-rooted results
(most `*:list` tools) never advertise it, so the SDK never installs a
validator for them and this class of bug can't manifest there. Any tool
declaring `result: z.object({...})` is a candidate; `work_items:burn_down`
is the one that got caught because its census payload is deeply nested and
never wins against JSON on size.

## What's still NOT covered (by design, not a live bug today)

- A caller that does **not** opt in (`_meta.structured` unset) still never
  gets `structuredContent`, and the SDK will still throw for them if the
  tool has `outputSchema`. This is the accepted P-010 trade-off (most agent
  callers never want the extra JSON), not something this fix changes. If a
  new caller class needs this and can't opt in per-call, the durable fix is
  a connection-level flag (`?structured=1` on the MCP URL) consulted when
  computing `tools/list`, so `outputSchema` is only advertised to
  connections that will always receive `structuredContent`.
- The `delta`/`not_modified` early-return branches in `serializeToolResponse`
  never attach `structuredContent` either. No registered tool today combines
  an object-rooted `result` with a `delta` capability, so this is dormant —
  but it would need the same treatment if one ever does.

## Symptom to recognize

Any MCP client using the reference TypeScript/Python SDK's `Client` class,
calling a tool with an **object-rooted `result` schema**, gets
`"Tool X has an output schema but did not return structured content"` even
though the call otherwise "worked" server-side. Check: did the caller set
`_meta.structured: true`? If yes and it still throws, check whether
`chosen.format` resolved to `'json'` for that payload shape — that was this
bug's exact trigger.
